target_customer: Police, fire and public safety agencies that handle 911 calls
problem: First responders often arrive without good information on a scene or its exact location; Paladin sends a drone ahead to stream live video.
business_model: Drone as first responder hardware and software sold to public safety agencies, likely subscription based
product_category: Drone as first responder (DFR) systems for public safety

founders.name: Divyaditya Shrivastava
education: UC Berkeley (student at founding, per Police1)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (May 2019) notes he is a recreational drone pilot. Idea came after a family friend's home burned down.

founders.name: Trevor Pennypacker
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by TechCrunch (May 2019) and InnovationMap (Oct 2024); not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous launch from a dock, reliable video streaming and FAA airspace compliance with consumer DJI drones in 2018 and 2019 was hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with agency dispatch and airspace waivers create switching costs, but reliance on DJI hardware left the product exposed and many drone firms entered later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Paladin used DJI drones at first and in 2026 launched a non-DJI platform (Knighthawk 2.0) per DroneXL via search; many rivals (Skydio, BRINC, Flock) entered DFR in the 2020s.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (May 2019) reports average emergency response time of 8 to 15 minutes and firefighters saying 911 location data is unreliable about 70 percent of the time.

branding.name_origin: Police1 says Paladin alludes to someone who fights for a cause, echoing heroic knights, and the company sees itself as a defender of public safety.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven public safety voice: First Eyes on Scene Before Units Arrive

branding.brand_signature: Knight-themed product names such as Knighthawk and Watchtower

brand_strength.rationale: Coherent knight-themed product naming and trade press coverage, but no evidence of broad consumer awareness.

outcome_analysis: Paladin raised a 1.3 million dollar seed after YC in 2019 and piloted with a Houston area police department. A 5.2 million dollar seed followed in October 2024 as drone as first responder programs spread among police departments. It remains active and the company reports 200K plus flights on its site, but funding history is thin and growth is still early.
notes: Competitors left empty: no source dated within a few months of the Summer 2018 batch naming rivals was found; the earliest relevant item found (Firehouse, July 2019, Phirst Technologies and FlytBase) is about a year after the batch. A Series A of 17 million dollars in September 2025 appears only on aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked, ZoomInfo) with differing labels and no primary release, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. A pay dispute lawsuit with a former VP of Sales was reported in December 2025 via search summary. The co-founder Pennypacker's education and employers were not found.
